advances: A restriction of the whole-fiber decomposition method for one actual compatible three-fiber body and one tested cap through its centroid. The balanced peeling class allowing densities to vary within each fiber has different hypotheses.

proof:
At each extreme base the hull has exactly the specified extreme fiber. At base $1$, a convex combination has equal weights on the endpoints. Their mean slice is $(K_0+K_2)/2=K_0\subseteq K_1$, so the section there is exactly $K_1$. The hull projects onto $[0,2]$ and is full-dimensional. The three positive volumes are $1,3/2,1$, and the fiber means in $x_1$ are $1/2,3/4,1/2$. Therefore the total mass is $7/2$, the base mean is $1$, and the mean in $x_1$ is $(1/2+(3/2)(3/4)+1/2)/(7/2)=17/28$. The other continuous coordinates all have mean $1/2$. Every fiber has mass below $M/2$.

Let $(m_0,m_1,m_2)$ be the three masses of a nonzero component. If its base centroid is $0$ or $2$, it is supported on that extreme fiber, whose mean $x_1=1/2$ violates the sign requirement. The integer base centroid must therefore be $1$, so $m_0=m_2=m$. Its unnormalized cap-coordinate moment is $(4m_1-6m)/28$. The moment condition forces $m_1\ge3m/2$. Across the components the sums of $m$ and $m_1$ are $1$ and $3/2$. All individual excesses $m_1-3m/2$ are nonnegative with sum zero, so each is zero. As the densities are constant on each whole fiber, the mass vector $m(1,3/2,1)$ means the component measure is exactly $m\mu$. In particular its mass is positive only when $m>0$, and its entire centroid is $g$.

For a positive submeasure $\sigma\le\mu$ with masses $b_z$, total $m_\sigma$ and centroid $g=(1,g_x)$, its positive-mass conditional centroids belong to $\mathsf M_{b_z}(K_z)$. The proof of dfd25e72c1f45a4e establishes convexity of the positive-root lift itself. Averaging with coefficients $b_z/m_\sigma$ places $g_x$ in the original middle-fiber metronoid of mass $\bigl(\sum_z b_z^{1+1/d}/m_\sigma\bigr)^d$. The selected trace of $H$ is a closed halfspace containing $g_x$, so 6769574fc1bd9f8d yields a lower bound on the actual middle trace equal to that mass times $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. This mass is $m_\sigma/N_{\mathrm{eff}}(\sigma)$ with $N_{\mathrm{eff}}(\sigma)=(\sum_z (b_z/m_\sigma)^{1+1/d})^{-d}$. For the proportional components these probabilities are unchanged. The mass budgets scale with $c_j$, and all output traces coincide. The sum of the numerical budgets is the original budget because $\sum_j c_j=1$.

For the original masses $a_z\in\{1,3/2,1\}$, the formula for $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ follows by substitution. Since $\sum_z a_z^{1+1/d}\le (3/2)^{1/d}M$, one has $N_{\mathrm{eff}}\ge M/(3/2)=7/3>2$. At $d=1$, $M^2/[2+(3/2)^2]=49/17$.

statement:
For each $d\ge1$, let $Q=[0,1]^{d-1}$ with the point convention for $d=1$. Take the convex hull of the lifted fibers $K_0=K_2=[0,1]\times Q$ and $K_1=[0,3/2]\times Q$ at integer bases $0,1,2$. Their summed $d$-volume $\mu$ has mass $M=7/2$ and centroid $g=(1,17/28,1/2,\ldots,1/2)$. Test the closed cap $H=\{x_1\ge17/28\}$. In every finite decomposition $\mu=\sum_j\mu_j$ into nonzero positive measures whose densities are constant on each whole fiber, if each component has integer base centroid and nonnegative mean $x_1-17/28$, then $\mu_j=c_j\mu$ for some $c_j>0$. Every such component has the same effective count
$$
N_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{M^{d+1}}{[\,2+(3/2)^{1+1/d}\,]^d}\ge7/3>2,
$$
equal to $49/17$ for $d=1$, and the same centroid and output fiber. The componentwise own-fiber root bounds have the original numerical coefficients scaled by $c_j$, so their numerical sum recovers the original bound.
title: Whole-fiber reweightings can force every integer-centered component to be proportional
